protocols.analysis: Three fresh baseline and exact final analyzer processes in ABBAAB order; same frozen 865-file SDK source census and exact diagnostic digest. No owned builds/native tests overlap. Earlier measurements remain in the CSV; the final analyzer includes reviewed exception-flow corrections. The final standard-conversion guard was qualified by another three baseline/accepted processes; the first review rerun remains labeled analysis-qualified-before-conversion-guard.
protocols.generation: Three fresh baseline and exact accepted payload processes in ABBAAB order; 16/64/256-type corpora warm at least 1.5 seconds before seven timed runs. Every measured result checks diagnostics, count and complete sorted source digest outside the timed/allocation interval. Odin uses Int32-backed enum keys and independently requires every owner, dictionary field, rewrite edit and capture/restore accessor. Historical count-only and unsupported-key observations remain labeled in the CSV and legacy summaries. First-execution observations are not whole-build timings.
protocols.ordering: Three fresh processes; seven calibrated alternating before/after rounds, each batch at least 20ms. Baseline is the prior stable LINQ expression, compiled in the probe against the same symbol APIs. Deep chains use cached buckets; shallow hierarchies retain the stable sort after the unconditional-bucket caller regression.
protocols.admission: Three fresh processes; seven calibrated alternating rounds at four source sizes and two subject sizes, with slash/backslash forms. Baseline is the former nested LINQ predicate; candidate links the actual audit implementation. Required suffix anchors are fixed at nine. Large-set membership is linear in sources plus subjects, while small sets have a bounded linear scan.
protocols.scope: Timings are host observations, not Unity editor/player build-time guarantees. Shared semantic binding can move between analyzer telemetry callbacks. Warm and first-execution results differ; small accepted WProto controls regress and are disclosed. Broad issue #1200 remains open. The unchanged enum control varies up to 9.8% warm and 21.3% on first execution in this rerun, so small ratios should not be interpreted as causal improvements. The earlier analysis ratio 0.949 is preserved alongside the first review rerun ratio 0.749; the final conversion-guard ratio is 0.820.
protocols.sources: Probe sources are formatted standalone reproductions; project XML preserves the captured configuration. The controls probe separately exercises foreign subjects while retaining every required anchor, small/large branches, case sensitivity, duplicate inputs and separator forms.

rejected.unconditionalBuckets: At 256 contracts, isolated warm medians: baseline 45.4755ms; unconditional buckets 57.5466ms; original-sort control retaining other optimizations 37.4553ms. Final adaptive implementation restores the shallow path.
rejected.enumAttributeNameChecks: 256 enums regress 5.53% warm and 31.82% on first execution; candidate removed and original source/binary retained.
rejected.unconditionalAuditHashing: Earlier nine-subject/512-source control regressed 27.7%; the accepted implementation uses a bounded small-set path.

reproduction: Place each formatted probe source at its original Program.cs or Admission.cs path under the matching ignored generator-performance project and write its recorded project XML.
Populate baseline payloads from baselineCommit and current payloads from the recorded source revision; verify their SHA-256 values before timing.
Generate SDK audit source/reference/symbol manifests with the editor source check; compare all recorded source hashes before reusing the analysis census.
For the generation probe, write the captured Odin stub content to its recorded path. Runtime attribute and migration sources are read from the repository.
Use separate output directories and fresh processes for each payload variant. No owned build or native test may overlap a timing capture.
The controls probe invokes the real audit phase and its original expression over deliberately valid and invalid small/large corpora.
